newsitem.title: USA: NCAA BASKETBALL-ARIZONA GUARD SIMON TO RETURN FOR SENIOR SEASON.
newsitem.headline: NCAA BASKETBALL-ARIZONA GUARD SIMON TO RETURN FOR SENIOR SEASON.

text.p: University of Arizona junior guard Miles Simon, the Most Valuable Player of this year's NCAA basketball tournament Final Four, announced Friday that he would return for his senior season.

"We are thrilled that Miles has decided to return to the University of Arizona for his senior season," coach Lute Olson said. "In the end, I thought his closeness to the team would be a deciding factor -- and it certainly was in his case."

Simon missed the first 11 games of the 1996-97 season due to an academic suspension, but averaged 18.4 points, 4.2 assists and 4.1 rebounds per game to lead the Wildcats to their first national championship.
Simon averaged 22 points in the NCAA Tournament and scored 30 points in the 84-79 championship game win over Kentucky.

Simon's return means that Arizona will see all five of this year's starters back for the 1997-98 campaign. The last NCAA champions that had all five starters return to defend the title was the 1967-68 UCLA Bruins.
"I am looking forward to next season and playing with this group of guys," said Simon in a refreshing change from the dash for NBA cash being made by so many college underclassmen in recent years.
"After experiencing all the excitement of what we accomplished in the NCAA Tournament this year, it was difficult to think about maybe missing out on it again next season," Simon said.
"When it came right down to it, I am having fun in college and I wanted to get a chance to go after a second national championship."
